passage: Every spring she left the fallen pears beneath the tree. By autumn the soil was darker where they had softened.
Removing the dam helped fish move upstream, yet the interview described the pond as a refuge for nesting birds.
The stones seemed to hold my mother's silence. I mean this as a way of describing my memory, not a claim about geology.
The article measured growth, while my grandfather spoke about patience. I am beginning to see that they answer different questions.
The author writes, 'I cannot tell whether the forest is recovering or changing.' My field notes concern a different forest.
I have permission to describe the ceremony but not to reproduce the words spoken there.
A line of ants disappeared into the crack. I counted eleven returning with fragments of leaves.
The same porch light that makes me feel safer draws moths away from the dark garden.
At first I called the garden wild and controlled. Those words now refer to different scales: the paths are planned, but the seedlings spread beyond them.
My next step is to compare the dates in the two sources before I decide whether their accounts conflict.
